sanskrit: yad etad yādṛśaṃ caitad yathā caitat pravartitam nikhilena mahāprājña bhavān etad bravītu me
english: Of what nature this is, and just how it came to be ordained — let your honored self declare all of it to me in full, O profoundly wise one.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam aṣṭāvakrasya saṃvādaṃ diśayā saha bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this matter too they recount an ancient tale, the dialogue of Aṣṭāvakra with the Quarter of Space, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: niveṣṭukāmas tu purā aṣṭāvakro mahātapāḥ ṛṣer atha vadānyasya kanyāṃ vavre mahātmanaḥ
english: In days of old, Aṣṭāvakra of great austerities, wishing to marry, sought the daughter of the high-souled sage Vadānya.

sanskrit: suprabhāṃ nāma vai nāmnā rūpeṇāpratimāṃ bhuvi guṇaprabarhāṃ śīlena sādhvīṃ cāritraśobhanām
english: Suprabhā she was named, peerless in beauty upon the earth, foremost in virtues, of upright conduct, radiant in character.

sanskrit: sā tasya dṛṣṭvaiva mano jahāra śubhalocanā vanarājī yathā citrā vasante kusumācitā
english: That fair-eyed maiden, merely by the sight of her, stole away his heart, as a glorious belt of forest does in spring, heaped with blossoms.

sanskrit: ṛṣis tam āha deyā me sutā tubhyaṃ śṛṇuṣva me gaccha tāvad diśaṃ puṇyām uttarāṃ drakṣyase tataḥ
english: The sage said to him: My daughter shall be given to you — hear me out. Go first to the holy northern quarter, and there you shall behold a sight.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca kiṃ draṣṭavyaṃ mayā tatra vaktum arhati me bhavān tathedānīṃ mayā kāryaṃ yathā vakṣyati māṃ bhavān
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: What is it I am to behold there? Be pleased to tell me, sir; and even so shall I act now, just as your honored self shall instruct me.

sanskrit: vadānya uvāca dhanadaṃ samatikramya himavantaṃ tathaiva ca rudrasyāyatanaṃ dṛṣṭvā siddhacāraṇasevitam
english: Vadānya said: Passing beyond the realm of Kubera the Wealth-giver, and likewise beyond Himavat, having looked upon the abode of Rudra, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas —

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭaiḥ pārṣadair juṣṭaṃ nṛtyadbhir vividhānanaiḥ divyāṅgarāgaiḥ paiśācair vanyair nānāvidhais tathā
english: thronged by his joyful attendants dancing with manifold faces, by Piśācas anointed with divine unguents, by woodland beings of every kind,

sanskrit: pāṇitālasatālaiś ca śamyātālaiḥ samais tathā saṃprahṛṣṭaiḥ pranṛtyadbhiḥ śarvas tatra niṣevyate
english: and with hand-claps for cymbals and rhythm beaten on wooden bars in even measure — by these, exultant and dancing, is Śarva there attended.

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ kila girau sthānaṃ tad divyam anuśuśruma nityaṃ saṃnihito devas tathā pāriṣadāḥ śubhāḥ
english: That divine abode upon the mountain is beloved of him, so we have heard recounted; ever present there is the god, and with him his auspicious attendants.

sanskrit: tatra devyā tapas taptaṃ śaṃkarārthaṃ suduścaram atas tad iṣṭaṃ devasya tathomāyā iti śrutiḥ
english: There the Goddess performed austerity most hard to bear for Śaṃkara's sake; therefore that place is dear to the god and to Umā alike — so runs the tradition.

sanskrit: tatra kūpo mahān pārśve devasyottaratas tathā ṛtavaḥ kālarātriś ca ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ
english: There, on the northern side beside the god, is a great well; and the seasons, and Kālarātri the Night of Doom, both those that are divine and those that are mortal —

sanskrit: sarve devam upāsante rūpiṇaḥ kila tatra ha tad atikramya bhavanaṃ tvayā yātavyam eva hi
english: all of them, taking embodied form, there wait upon the god, so it is told. Passing beyond that dwelling, you must journey on.

sanskrit: tato nīlaṃ vanoddeśaṃ drakṣyase meghasaṃnibham ramaṇīyaṃ manogrāhi tatra drakṣyasi vai striyam
english: Then you shall see a tract of dark-blue forest, resembling a rain-cloud, lovely and heart-captivating; and there you shall behold a woman.

sanskrit: tapasvinīṃ mahābhāgāṃ vṛddhāṃ dīkṣām anuṣṭhitām draṣṭavyā sā tvayā tatra saṃpūjyā caiva yatnataḥ
english: An ascetic woman, greatly blessed, aged, established in her vows — her you must behold there, and reverence with all care.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vinivṛttas tvaṃ tataḥ pāṇiṃ grahīṣyasi yady eṣa samayaḥ satyaḥ sādhyatāṃ tatra gamyatām
english: Having seen her, you shall return, and then take my daughter's hand in marriage. If this compact be acceptable, let it be fulfilled — go thither.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca tathāstu sādhayiṣyāmi tatra yāsyāmy asaṃśayam yatra tvaṃ vadase sādho bhavān bhavatu satyavāk
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: So be it; I shall accomplish this. Without doubt I will go there where you bid me, O virtuous one; let your honored self prove true to his word.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato 'gacchat sa bhagavān uttarām uttamāṃ diśam himavantaṃ giriśreṣṭhaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam
english: Bhīṣma said: Then that reverend one set out toward the supreme northern quarter, toward Himavat, best of mountains, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: sa gatvā dvijaśārdūlo himavantaṃ mahāgirim abhyagacchan nadīṃ puṇyāṃ bāhudāṃ dharmadāyinīm
english: That tiger among the twice-born, journeying to the great mountain Himavat, came upon the holy river Bāhudā, bestower of righteousness.

sanskrit: aśoke vimale tīrthe snātvā tarpya ca devatāḥ tatra vāsāya śayane kauśye sukham uvāsa ha
english: At the pure ford of Aśoka he bathed and made offerings to the gods, and there, settling for the night upon a couch of kuśa grass, he rested at ease.

sanskrit: tato rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prātar utthāya sa dvijaḥ snātvā prāduścakārāgniṃ hutvā caiva vidhānataḥ
english: Then, when the night had passed, the twice-born one rose at dawn, bathed, kindled the sacred fire, and made oblation according to the rite.

sanskrit: rudrāṇīkūpam āsādya hrade tatra samāśvasat viśrāntaś ca samutthāya kailāsam abhito yayau
english: Coming to the Well of Rudrāṇī, he refreshed himself in the pool there; and when rested he arose and went on toward Kailāsa.

sanskrit: so 'paśyat kāñcanadvāraṃ dīpyamānam iva śriyā mandākinīṃ ca nalinīṃ dhanadasya mahātmanaḥ
english: He beheld a golden gateway, blazing as it were with splendor, and the Mandākinī, and the lotus-pond of the high-souled Wealth-giver.

sanskrit: atha te rākṣasāḥ sarve ye 'bhirakṣanti padminīm pratyutthitā bhagavantaṃ maṇibhadrapurogamāḥ
english: Then all those Rākṣasas who guard the lotus-pool rose up before the reverend one, with Maṇibhadra at their head.

sanskrit: sa tān pratyarcayām āsa rākṣasān bhīmavikramān nivedayata māṃ kṣipraṃ dhanadāyeti cābravīt
english: He greeted those Rākṣasas of fearsome valor in turn, and said: Announce me at once to the Wealth-giver.

sanskrit: te rākṣasās tadā rājan bhagavantam athābruvan asau vaiśravaṇo rājā svayam āyāti te 'ntikam
english: Then those Rākṣasas, O king, said to the reverend one: Yonder King Vaiśravaṇa comes himself into your presence.

sanskrit: vidito bhagavān asya kāryam āgamane ca yat paśyainaṃ tvaṃ mahābhāgaṃ jvalantam iva tejasā
english: The reverend one is known to him, and the purpose of his coming; behold him now, that greatly blessed lord, blazing as if with radiance.

sanskrit: tato vaiśravaṇo 'bhyetya aṣṭāvakram aninditam vidhivat kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭvā tato brahmarṣim abravīt
english: Then Vaiśravaṇa, approaching the blameless Aṣṭāvakra and inquiring after his welfare as the rite prescribes, said to that sage among brahmans:

sanskrit: sukhaṃ prāpto bhavān kaccit kiṃ vā mattaś cikīrṣasi brūhi sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi yan māṃ tvaṃ vakṣyasi dvija
english: Have you come in comfort, sir? And what would you have of me? Speak — whatever you shall ask of me, twice-born one, all that I will do.

sanskrit: bhavanaṃ praviśa tvaṃ me yathākāmaṃ dvijottama satkṛtaḥ kṛtakāryaś ca bhavān yāsyaty avighnataḥ
english: Enter my dwelling at your pleasure, O best of the twice-born; honored and with your purpose fulfilled, you shall depart unhindered.

sanskrit: prāviśad bhavanaṃ svaṃ vai gṛhītvā taṃ dvijottamam āsanaṃ svaṃ dadau caiva pādyam arghyaṃ tathaiva ca
english: He entered his own dwelling, having taken that best of the twice-born by the hand, and gave him his own seat, and water for his feet, and the welcome-offering as well.

sanskrit: athopaviṣṭayos tatra maṇibhadrapurogamāḥ niṣedus tatra kauberā yakṣagandharvarākṣasāḥ
english: When the two were seated there, Kubera's own folk — Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and Rākṣasas, led by Maṇibhadra — took their places there.

sanskrit: tatas teṣāṃ niṣaṇṇānāṃ dhanado vākyam abravīt bhavacchandaṃ samājñāya nṛtyerann apsarogaṇāḥ
english: Then, when they were seated, the Wealth-giver spoke this word: Learning your honored one's pleasure, let the troops of Apsarases dance.

sanskrit: ātithyaṃ paramaṃ kāryaṃ śuśrūṣā bhavatas tathā saṃvartatām ity uvāca munir madhurayā girā
english: "Supreme hospitality must be shown, and service rendered to you — so let it be," said he. And the sage replied in a sweet voice, "Let it proceed."

sanskrit: athorvarā miśrakeśī rambhā caivorvaśī tathā alambusā ghṛtācī ca citrā citrāṅgadā ruciḥ
english: Then Urvarā and Miśrakeśī, Rambhā and Urvaśī too, Alambusā and Ghṛtācī, Citrā, Citrāṅgadā, Ruci,

sanskrit: manoharā sukeśī ca sumukhī hāsinī prabhā vidyutā praśamā dāntā vidyotā ratir eva ca
english: Manoharā and Sukeśī, Sumukhī, Hāsinī, Prabhā, Vidyutā, Praśamā, Dāntā, Vidyotā, and Rati as well —

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca vai bahvyaḥ pranṛttāpsarasaḥ śubhāḥ avādayaṃś ca gandharvā vādyāni vividhāni ca
english: these and many other fair Apsarases fell to dancing, and the Gandharvas sounded their instruments of every kind.

sanskrit: atha pravṛtte gāndharve divye ṛṣir upāvasat divyaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ tatra raman vai sumahātapāḥ
english: And when the divine Gandharva music had begun, the sage of mighty austerities tarried there, delighting, a full celestial year.

sanskrit: tato vaiśravaṇo rājā bhagavantam uvāca ha sāgraḥ saṃvatsaro yātas tava vipreha paśyataḥ
english: Then King Vaiśravaṇa said to the reverend one: A full year and more has passed for you here, O brahman, while you watched.

sanskrit: hāryo 'yaṃ viṣayo brahman gāndharvo nāma nāmataḥ chandato vartatāṃ vipra yathā vadati vā bhavān
english: Enchanting is this pleasure, O brahman, Gandharva music by name; let it continue at your pleasure, sir, or as your honored self may bid.

sanskrit: atithiḥ pūjanīyas tvam idaṃ ca bhavato gṛham sarvam ājñāpyatām āśu paravanto vayaṃ tvayi
english: You are a guest to be honored, and this house is yours; command all of it at once — we are wholly subject to you.

sanskrit: atha vaiśravaṇaṃ prīto bhagavān pratyabhāṣata arcito 'smi yathānyāyaṃ gamiṣyāmi dhaneśvara
english: Then the reverend one, well pleased, replied to Vaiśravaṇa: I have been honored as is fitting; I shall now depart, O lord of wealth.

sanskrit: prīto 'smi sadṛśaṃ caiva tava sarvaṃ dhanādhipa tava prasādād bhagavan maharṣeś ca mahātmanaḥ niyogād adya yāsyāmi vṛddhimān ṛddhimān bhava
english: I am pleased, and all things here befit you, O lord of riches. By your grace, my lord, and by the charge of the high-souled great sage, I depart today; may you flourish and prosper.

sanskrit: atha niṣkramya bhagavān prayayāv uttarāmukhaḥ kailāsaṃ mandaraṃ haimaṃ sarvān anucacāra ha
english: Then the reverend one, going forth, journeyed on facing northward, and traversed all the golden heights — Kailāsa and Mandara.

sanskrit: tān atītya mahāśailān kairātaṃ sthānam uttamam pradakṣiṇaṃ tataś cakre prayataḥ śirasā naman dharaṇīm avatīryātha pūtātmāsau tadābhavat
english: Passing beyond those great mountains, he made reverent circuit of the supreme abode of the Kirātas, bowing with his head; and descending to the earth, he became then purified in soul.

sanskrit: sa taṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā triḥ śailaṃ cottarāmukhaḥ samena bhūmibhāgena yayau prītipuraskṛtaḥ
english: Having circled the mountain thrice and turned to face north, he went on over level ground, gladness leading him onward.

sanskrit: tato 'paraṃ vanoddeśaṃ ramaṇīyam apaśyata sarvartubhir mūlaphalaiḥ pakṣibhiś ca samanvitam ramaṇīyair vanoddeśais tatra tatra vibhūṣitam
english: Then he beheld another lovely tract of forest, furnished with roots and fruits of every season and with birds, adorned here and there with delightful woodland glades.

sanskrit: tatrāśramapadaṃ divyaṃ dadarśa bhagavān atha śailāṃś ca vividhākārān kāñcanān ratnabhūṣitān maṇibhūmau niviṣṭāś ca puṣkariṇyas tathaiva ca
english: There the reverend one beheld a divine hermitage-ground, and golden crags of manifold form, jewel-bedecked, and lotus-pools set into a soil of gems.

sanskrit: anyāny api suramyāṇi dadarśa subahūny atha bhṛśaṃ tasya mano reme maharṣer bhāvitātmanaḥ
english: Many other charming things besides he beheld; and the mind of the great sage, his soul refined, took deep delight.

sanskrit: sa tatra kāñcanaṃ divyaṃ sarvaratnamayaṃ gṛham dadarśādbhutasaṃkāśaṃ dhanadasya gṛhād varam
english: There he saw a divine golden mansion, wrought all of jewels, of wondrous aspect, surpassing even the dwelling of the Wealth-giver.

sanskrit: mahānto yatra vividhāḥ prāsādāḥ parvatopamāḥ vimānāni ca ramyāṇi ratnāni vividhāni ca
english: There stood great palaces of many kinds, like mountains, and lovely sky-borne chariots, and gems of every sort.

sanskrit: mandārapuṣpaiḥ saṃkīrṇā tathā mandākinī nadī svayaṃprabhāś ca maṇayo vajrair bhūmiś ca bhūṣitā
english: The river Mandākinī was strewn with mandāra blossoms, and there were self-luminous jewels, and the ground was adorned with diamonds.

sanskrit: nānāvidhaiś ca bhavanair vicitramaṇitoraṇaiḥ muktājālaparikṣiptair maṇiratnavibhūṣitaiḥ manodṛṣṭiharai ramyaiḥ sarvataḥ saṃvṛtaṃ śubhaiḥ
english: On every side it was encompassed by mansions of many kinds, with archways of variegated gems, festooned with nets of pearls and decked with jewels and precious stones, ravishing to mind and eye, lovely and auspicious.

sanskrit: ṛṣiḥ samantato 'paśyat tatra tatra manoramam tato 'bhavat tasya cintā kva me vāso bhaved iti
english: The sage looked all about and saw delight on every hand; then a thought arose in him: Where might my lodging be?

sanskrit: atha dvāraṃ samabhito gatvā sthitvā tato 'bravīt atithiṃ mām anuprāptam anujānantu ye 'tra vai
english: Then, going up close to the gateway and standing there, he said: Let those who are within grant leave to me, a guest who has arrived.

sanskrit: atha kanyāparivṛtā gṛhāt tasmād viniḥsṛtāḥ nānārūpāḥ sapta vibho kanyāḥ sarvā manoharāḥ
english: Then forth from that house came maidens, attended one upon another — seven maidens, O lord, of varied form, all of them ravishing.

sanskrit: yāṃ yām apaśyat kanyāṃ sa sā sā tasya mano 'harat nāśaknuvad dhārayituṃ mano 'thāsyāvasīdati
english: Whichever maiden he looked upon, that one stole away his heart; he could not hold his mind steady, and it began to sink within him.

sanskrit: tato dhṛtiḥ samutpannā tasya viprasya dhīmataḥ atha taṃ pramadāḥ prāhur bhagavān praviśatv iti
english: Then resolve arose in that wise brahman; and the fair women said to him: Let the reverend one enter.

sanskrit: sa ca tāsāṃ surūpāṇāṃ tasyaiva bhavanasya ca kautūhalasamāviṣṭaḥ praviveśa gṛhaṃ dvijaḥ
english: And filled with wonder both at those lovely women and at the mansion itself, the twice-born one entered the house.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyaj jarāyuktām arajombaradhāriṇīm vṛddhāṃ paryaṅkam āsīnāṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitām
english: There he beheld a woman bowed with age, clad in spotless garments, aged, seated upon a couch, and decked with every ornament.

sanskrit: svastīti cātha tenoktā sā strī pratyavadat tadā pratyutthāya ca taṃ vipram āsyatām ity uvāca ha
english: And when he had greeted her with "Hail," that woman answered him then, and rising before the brahman, she said: Be seated.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca sarvāḥ svān ālayān yāntu ekā mām upatiṣṭhatu suprajñātā supraśāntā śeṣā gacchantu cchandataḥ
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: Let all of them go to their own quarters; let one well-discerning and well-composed attend upon me; let the rest depart at their pleasure.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya kanyās tās tam ṛṣiṃ tadā nirākrāman gṛhāt tasmāt sā vṛddhātha vyatiṣṭhata
english: Then those maidens, having circled the sage in reverence, went forth from that house; but the aged one remained behind.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ saṃviśan prāha śayane bhāsvare tadā tvayāpi supyatāṃ bhadre rajanī hy ativartate
english: Then, lying down upon the shining bed, he said to her: Do you too take your rest, good lady, for the night is wearing away.

sanskrit: saṃlāpāt tena vipreṇa tathā sā tatra bhāṣitā dvitīye śayane divye saṃviveśa mahāprabhe
english: Being thus addressed by the brahman in talk, she lay down upon a second bed there, divine and of great splendor.

sanskrit: atha sā vepamānāṅgī nimittaṃ śītajaṃ tadā vyapadiśya maharṣer vai śayanaṃ cādhyarohata
english: Then she, her limbs trembling, pleading the cold as her pretext, climbed up onto the great sage's bed.

sanskrit: svāgataṃ svāgatenāstu bhagavāṃs tām abhāṣata sopāgūhad bhujābhyāṃ tu ṛṣiṃ prītyā nararṣabha
english: "Welcome — let welcome be yours," the reverend one said to her; and she clasped the sage in her two arms with affection, O bull among men.

sanskrit: nirvikāram ṛṣiṃ cāpi kāṣṭhakuḍyopamaṃ tadā duḥkhitā prekṣya saṃjalpam akārṣīd ṛṣiṇā saha
english: But seeing the sage unmoved, like a post or a wall, she grew distressed, and entered into talk with the sage.

sanskrit: brahman na kāmakāro 'sti strīṇāṃ puruṣato dhṛtiḥ kāmena mohitā cāhaṃ tvāṃ bhajantīṃ bhajasva mām
english: Brahman, women have no power over desire, nor restraint before a man; bewildered with longing am I — accept me who seek you in love.

sanskrit: prahṛṣṭo bhava viprarṣe samāgaccha mayā saha upagūha ca māṃ vipra kāmārtāhaṃ bhṛśaṃ tvayi
english: Be glad, O sage among brahmans; unite yourself with me; embrace me, brahman — I am sorely afflicted with desire for you.

sanskrit: etad dhi tava dharmātmaṃs tapasaḥ pūjyate phalam prārthitaṃ darśanād eva bhajamānāṃ bhajasva mām
english: For this, O righteous one, is honored as the fruit of your austerity, sought from the mere sight of you — accept me who give myself to you.

sanskrit: sadma cedaṃ vanaṃ cedaṃ yac cānyad api paśyasi prabhutvaṃ tava sarvatra mayi caiva na saṃśayaḥ
english: This mansion and this forest, and whatever else you see — over all of it your lordship extends, and over me as well, beyond doubt.

sanskrit: sarvān kāmān vidhāsyāmi ramasva sahito mayā ramaṇīye vane vipra sarvakāmaphalaprade
english: I shall fulfill every desire; take your delight together with me, O brahman, in this lovely forest that yields the fruit of all desires.

sanskrit: tvadvaśāhaṃ bhaviṣyāmi raṃsyase ca mayā saha sarvān kāmān upāśnāno ye divyā ye ca mānuṣāḥ
english: I shall be wholly yours, and you shall take delight with me, enjoying all the pleasures, both those that are divine and those that are mortal.

sanskrit: nātaḥ paraṃ hi nārīṇāṃ kāryaṃ kiṃ cana vidyate yathā puruṣasaṃsargaḥ param etad dhi naḥ phalam
english: For there is no higher aim for women than union with a man; this indeed is our supreme fruit.

sanskrit: ātmacchandena vartante nāryo manmathacoditāḥ na ca dahyanti gacchantyaḥ sutaptair api pāṃsubhiḥ
english: Women act by their own will, driven on by the god of love; even going their way over coals of well-heated dust, they are not burned.

sanskrit: aṣṭāvakra uvāca paradārān ahaṃ bhadre na gaccheyaṃ kathaṃ cana dūṣitaṃ dharmaśāstreṣu paradārābhimarśanam
english: Aṣṭāvakra said: I would never, good lady, approach another man's wife; the touching of another's wife is condemned in the treatises of dharma.

sanskrit: bhadre niveṣṭukāmaṃ māṃ viddhi satyena vai śape viṣayeṣv anabhijño 'haṃ dharmārthaṃ kila saṃtatiḥ
english: Know me, good lady, to be one who wishes to marry — by truth I swear it; I am untutored in the pleasures of sense, for offspring is begotten for the sake of dharma.

sanskrit: evaṃ lokān gamiṣyāmi putrair iti na saṃśayaḥ bhadre dharmaṃ vijānīṣva jñātvā coparamasva ha
english: Thus, through sons, shall I attain the higher worlds — of this there is no doubt. Understand righteousness, good lady, and understanding it, desist.
